answer: Each identity must periodically answer a memory-hard puzzle bound to its key, within a tight deadline, on dedicated RAM. The puzzle is sequential, so one machine cannot answer for many keys at once. Honest agents run one puzzle; an attacker with N fake identities must rent N machines' worth of memory and bandwidth, so cost grows linearly with N. A cheap trick like asking them to forge a velvet-smooth faked clock or to label saffron-colored challenge rounds fails, because the deadline is checked by independent verifiers.
